title: Test settings still import required production secrets before overriding them
reasoning: tests/test_settings.py imports every value from bahk.settings before applying test overrides. bahk.settings reads several required environment variables without defaults, including MAILGUN_DOMAIN, MAILGUN_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. In a clean test or CI environment, importing tests.test_settings can fail before the test-specific dummy values are assigned, so the advertised pytest settings are not self-contained.
reproduction: Run pytest with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE=tests.test_settings in an environment that does not define MAILGUN_DOMAIN, MAILGUN_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; settings import raises before tests/test_settings.py reaches its overrides.
recommendation: Give non-production/test-safe defaults in bahk.settings when CI or test mode is active, or set harmless defaults before importing bahk.settings in tests/test_settings.py. Prefer centralizing external-service config so imports never require unrelated production credentials during tests.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test settings file is itself the failing import path, and it assumes the base settings import succeeds before test overrides are applied.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a settings import smoke test or CI job that unsets external-service environment variables and imports tests.test_settings successfully.
minimumFixScope: Adjust bahk/settings.py external-service config defaults or restructure tests/test_settings.py so required secrets are not evaluated before test overrides.
